summary: Defines new vCard properties and extends existing ones so that vCard and JSContact can express the same features. The new definitions are also meant to be useful in vCard alone. It updates RFC 6350, the vCard specification.

eli5.summary: Two address book formats spoke slightly different languages. This adds some missing words to the older one so both can say the same things.

questions: what new properties does rfc 9554 add to vcard
subtitle: New vCard properties, parameters and values so that vCard can carry everything JSContact can.

tldr.problem: JSContact introduces contact semantics that vCard cannot express, so converting between the two formats could lose information.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC extends the ADR and N properties, adds five properties (CREATED, GRAMGENDER, LANGUAGE, PRONOUNS, SOCIALPROFILE), ten parameters and two address type values.
tldr.outcome: Conversion between vCard and JSContact can avoid losing semantics, and the additions are also meant to be useful in vCard alone. It updates RFC 6350.

today: RFC 9554 is a Proposed Standard from May 2024 that updates RFC 6350. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why vCard Needed Extending
sections.content:
JSContact (RFC 9553) is meant as an alternative to vCard (RFC 6350) for contact and address book data. It brings new semantics that vCard and its extensions do not cover. RFC 9555 defines converting between the two with the goal of not losing any semantics.

To make that possible, this document defines a new set of vCard properties and extends existing definitions. It updates RFC 6350. The ABNF uses the notation of RFC 5234.
sections.eli5: Two forms for writing down a friend's details had different boxes. This RFC adds boxes to the old form so nothing gets lost when you copy between them.

sections.title: Richer Addresses and Names
sections.content:
The ADR property gets eleven new address components after the original seven: room, apartment, floor, street number, street name, building, block, subdistrict, district, landmark and direction. Implementations SHOULD write a combined value in the street component for backwards compatibility, and SHOULD ignore the street component on reads if any new component is present.

The N property gains a secondary surname component and a generation component (for markers such as II or Jr.). For compatibility, implementations SHOULD add such values to both the new and the old component, and on reading ignore the old value if an equal one is set in the new component. The RFC mentions this also supports formatting with the Unicode CLDR Person Name standard.

The SORT-AS parameter is unchanged, but the new name components also apply to it.
sections.eli5: The address form gets extra lines for things like floor and building, and the name form gets lines for a second family name and for 'Jr.'. The old lines are still filled in so old readers cope.

sections.title: New Properties
sections.content:
Five properties are added:

  • CREATED: when the vCard was created. Copying it across systems is not a new creation. Cardinality is at most one.
  • GRAMGENDER: the grammatical gender to use in salutations, from animate, common, feminine, inanimate, masculine, neuter or an IANA or x-name token. Multiple occurrences MUST be told apart by the LANGUAGE parameter.
  • LANGUAGE: the default language of text values in the vCard. A LANGUAGE parameter on a property takes precedence.
  • PRONOUNS: free-form text pronouns the contact chooses. Several may exist for different languages or preferences; same-language ones SHOULD use PREF.
  • SOCIALPROFILE: a URI (the default) or TEXT username for a social media profile. A TEXT value MUST come with the SERVICE-TYPE parameter. It replaces the experimental X-SOCIALPROFILE property that several implementations use.
sections.eli5: New boxes on the contact card: when it was made, how to address the person in grammar, which language it is in, which pronouns they like, and where their social profiles are.

sections.title: New Parameters and Values
sections.content:
Ten parameters can be attached to properties:

  • AUTHOR (a quoted URI) and AUTHOR-NAME (free text, not empty) identify who wrote a value.
  • CREATED gives a property's creation timestamp.
  • DERIVED set to true says a value is computed from other properties, for example FN from N, and clients MUST NOT update it.
  • LABEL holds a formatted address label for ADR. RFC 6350 mentioned it but it was never registered.
  • PHONETIC marks a value as the pronunciation of a same-named property, using ipa, jyut, piny or script. Both properties MUST share an ALTID.
  • SCRIPT gives a four-letter script subtag such as Latn, required with PHONETIC=script.
  • PROP-ID uniquely identifies a property among same-named siblings, 1 to 255 octets of letters, digits, hyphen and underscore.
  • SERVICE-TYPE and USERNAME name the online service and user for IMPP and SOCIALPROFILE.

Two new TYPE values for ADR are billing and delivery.
sections.eli5: Stickers you can put on any box: who wrote it, when, how to say it out loud, and an ID tag so you can tell two similar boxes apart.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
IANA has added the five properties to the vCard Properties registry and the ten parameters to the vCard Parameters registry. It has also added references to this RFC for ADR and N, the six GRAMGENDER values to the vCard Property Values registry, and the billing, delivery and PHONETIC values to the vCard Parameter Values registry.

The security considerations are those of Section 9 of RFC 6350, which apply unchanged.
sections.eli5: The official list of allowed boxes and stickers has been updated, and the same safety rules as before apply.
